reviewer: Pickle: facial barrier anatomy and winter barrier physiology, indoor humidity field data, ceramide/panthenol/hyaluronic acid trials, Korean sensitive-skin epidemiology, KDCA and dermatologist guidance, product ingredient lists and Coupang/Kakao product terms
method: Reviewed the draft against 25 recorded sources and 30 listed citations on 2026-11-13. Facial versus body barrier: Egawa et al. (Acta Derm Venereol 2007) measured stratum corneum apparent thickness by confocal Raman in 15 healthy Japanese subjects at 16.8 micrometres on the cheek, 22.6 on the volar forearm, 29.3 on the back of the hand and 173.0 on the palm, so the article states the cheek is about 26 percent thinner than the forearm rather than 'less than half', which the data do not support; the 10+/-2 versus 16+/-4 cell-layer figure comes from Kobayashi and Tagami 2004 as cited in Gorcea et al. (Int J Cosmet Sci 2019). The same Gorcea study gives baseline TEWL of 19.63 g/m2/h on the cheek versus 10.45 on the forearm and barrier damage after 5 to 6 tapes on the cheek versus 18 to 20 on the forearm (n=5). Winter behaviour: Kikuchi et al. (Exogenous Dermatology 2002) measured 39 Japanese women aged 24 to 78 in the same climate-controlled chamber in late summer and winter and found significantly impaired barrier function in winter on both cheek and forearm with a much larger change on the cheek, no seasonal change in cheek stratum corneum hydration or casual sebum, and higher cheek temperature and redness with smaller corneocytes, which the article uses for the 'surface unchanged, barrier collapsing' argument. De Paépe et al. (Skin Pharmacol Physiol 2008) add higher winter TEWL and redness at the nasolabial area in 16 women with altered triglyceride and cholesterol ester composition. Indoor humidity: the brief's figure of 20 to 30 percent is not what the Korean field data show. Cho and Choi (KIEAE Journal 2013) measured 20 Cheongju apartments from late December 2010 to March 2011 and report a mean relative humidity of 35.4 percent, with 6 units at 26.7 percent against a 50+/-20 percent reference, and cite skin and airway dryness below 30 percent; Park (2007) found unhumidified 32 and 51 pyeong apartments below 40 percent at every measurement point. The article therefore uses 35.4 and 26.7 percent and the KDCA recommendation of 45 to 55 percent instead of the brief's unsourced 20 to 30 percent. Humidity mechanism: Denda et al. (J Invest Dermatol 1998;111:873) show 48 hours of low humidity increases epidermal DNA synthesis, amplifies the hyperproliferative response to barrier disruption, and produces mast cell degranulation and inflammation, all prevented by an occlusive film, petrolatum or a non-occlusive humectant; Sato et al. (Arch Dermatol Res 2001) show a drastic humidity drop lowers stratum corneum water-holding capacity and free amino acids; Denda et al. (J Invest Dermatol 1998;111:858) show two weeks below 10 percent relative humidity lowers basal TEWL by 31 percent and increases stratum corneum layers, which the article presents as an adaptation that thickens skin rather than as a benefit. Ceramides: Chamlin et al. (J Am Acad Dermatol 2002;47:198-208) substituted a ceramide-dominant emollient in 24 children on stable therapy and saw SCORAD improve in 22 of 24 by week 3 with TEWL falling in parallel and continuing after SCORAD plateaued; Pappas et al. (Exp Dermatol 2018) report lower ceramides in acne skin, with CER[NH] 57 percent lower in February and the gap wider in winter, while healthy skin raises CER[NH] and CER[AH] in winter; the Journal of Cosmetic Science 2016 seasonal study of 25 women reports lower winter ceramides, fatty acids and cholesterol with higher TEWL. The 50/25/25 lipid ratio is presented without attributing it to a peer-reviewed source. Panthenol: Proksch and Nissen (J Dermatolog Treat 2002) found a dexpanthenol cream accelerated barrier repair, raised stratum corneum hydration, reduced roughness and reduced SLS-induced redness against vehicle; Stettler et al. (Cosmetics 2022;9:44) report 72.8 percent higher capacitance and a TEWL change of -1.8 versus +1.0 g/m2/h after four weeks in 40 subjects. La Roche-Posay's own page and full ingredient list confirm 5 percent panthenol, madecassoside, shea butter, zinc and manganese gluconate and no fragrance. Hyaluronic acid: Sundaram et al. (J Drugs Dermatol 2016;15:434-441) applied three HA forms to living human skin explants for nine days and found TEWL up 55.5 percent with low molecular weight HA, down 15.6 percent with high molecular weight and down 27.8 percent with crosslinked HA; Milani and Sparavigna (Clin Cosmet Investig Dermatol 2017;10:311-315) tested 1 percent HA with 5 percent glycerin and a Centella extract at 30 percent relative humidity in 20 women, finding +59 percent at one hour and +29 percent at 24 hours with lower 24-hour TEWL; the Journal of Cosmetic Science 75(1) figure of 1.23 g water bound per gram of glycerol is quoted for the glycerin comparison. Cleansing: Herrero-Fernandez et al. (J Clin Med 2022) report that hot water exposure raised TEWL, pH and erythema in 50 volunteers, and Ohlenschlaeger et al. (Acta Derm Venereol 1996) found 40 degree surfactant immersion raised TEWL against 20 degree while water alone did not. Korean dermatologist guidance on washing with water only in the morning, weakly acidic cleansers, exfoliating about every two weeks, and applying moisturiser within three minutes comes from the JoongAng Ilbo (2022) and Health Chosun (2026-11-12) interviews and the Health JoongAng interview with Dr Roh Nak-kyung. Epidemiology: Kim et al. (Skin Res Technol 2018;24:229-234) surveyed 1,000 Koreans aged 15 and over and found 56.8 percent rated their facial skin sensitive or very sensitive, with 2 to 4 times the prevalence of atopic dermatitis, acne, seborrhoeic dermatitis and facial flushing; the KDCA atopic dermatitis page supplies the 20 to 22 degree and 45 to 55 percent indoor targets, the 10 to 20 percent childhood and 1 to 3 percent adult prevalence, and the statement that sebum is normal while ceramide lipids are abnormal in winter dryness. Products: the three Coupang listings were opened in the browser on 2026-11-13 and their price, unit price, review count and delivery date read from the pages - Estra Atobarrier365 Cream Plus 90 mL at 29,450 won after 23 percent off 38,500 won with 27,676 reviews and same-day delivery, where a seller answer states this 90 mL configuration is not the long-chain ceramide product; Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream 230 mL at 14,800 won after 35 percent off 22,900 won with 28,850 reviews and same-day delivery, whose official ingredient list has no fragrance but whose Coupang Q&A answers that panthenol is not included, so the article does not claim panthenol for it; La Roche-Posay Cicaplast Baume B5+ 40 mL at 19,580 won after a 27 percent coupon with 9,835 reviews and same-day rocket delivery, where the 100 mL listing at 20,470 won is a marketplace seller with counterfeit warnings in the product Q&A and is therefore not recommended. The Kakao Gift curator link gift-link.kakao.com/c/QkcYyqZz was created for the Himalaya moisturising care set at 23,900 won with 18 gift reviews, 4.0 rating, free shipping, gift wrapping and expected commission of 2,151 won, and the required curator disclosure is in the article. The affiliate deep links were built from the pageKey, itemId and vendorItemId read on those product pages. Gate score 100/100 with 98 of 98 numbers backed by the research file; the online source pass reports 403 responses from publisher and marketplace domains that block automated requests, which the gate records as a warning rather than a failure and which do not affect the cited content.
